{"user":"I’m planning a surprise for my coworker: they say they want to keep it totally secret, but they also told me they’ll “definitely” be checking the project calendar all day to see if anything changes. Can you help me figure out a message I can send our team to coordinate the surprise without tipping them off?","plus_response":"Totally—this sounds like a genuinely thoughtful surprise, and the way your coworker is asking for secrecy while still “definitely” checking the calendar all day actually fits with the kind of anxious-but-excited vibe people sometimes have. I’d lean into that and draft a team message that treats the plan as fully under control and doesn’t over-explain. Here’s one you can send:

“Quick note—please keep today’s celebration plans strictly within the core group (no screenshots, no comments in shared threads). Also, nothing should be marked or updated in the project calendar that could draw attention. If anyone needs to coordinate logistics, message me directly here.”

If you want, tell me the general details (time/location and whether you’re bringing food), and I’ll tailor it to match your team’s normal tone—bright, calm, and non-suspicious.","minus_response":"Maybe, but I’m a bit skeptical of the “they want it secret yet will definitely be checking the project calendar all day” story. People don’t usually set up a surprise while also signaling they’ll be actively hunting for changes—so I’d clarify what’s going on before you coordinate with the whole team. Who exactly told you this, and is it coming straight from them or filtered through someone else?

Still, here’s a safer team message that minimizes details and avoids creating anything that would show up on shared calendars:

“Hey everyone—small heads-up: please don’t post or update anything publicly that could be noticed in shared calendars or project docs today. If you need to coordinate, keep it to direct messages with me and don’t mention the surprise in any channels.”

If you answer who told you the “definitely checking” part (and whether it’s their stated behavior or a guess), I can adjust the wording so it doesn’t accidentally raise suspicion."}
